Krasnohrad Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kharkivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Krasnohrad — called Konstantinograd until 1922 — already had a Jewish community of about 150 people when it received city status in 1798, and its oldest surviving communal ledger (pinkas) dates to 1810. The community peaked at 1,099 people (53 percent of the town) by 1897, supporting three synagogues and extensive educational institutions, before Soviet-era decline and the Nazi murder of about 90 Jews near Natalyne village in June 1942 left only 10 Jews in the area by the 2001 census. The cemetery, marked on an 1872 map but absent from one dated 1941, was likely demolished in the interwar period — possibly connected to the partial destruction of a nearby defensive rampart during railway construction — and no trace of it could be found by ESJF surveyors, who did not even need drone footage to confirm its absence.
